title: Creating Effective Solution Overview Diagrams
explanation: A solution overview diagram provides a high-level view of a system's architecture, showing the major components and their interactions. It is typically the first diagram stakeholders see and should communicate the essence of the solution clearly and concisely. This module covers the principles of creating effective solution overview diagrams for UK government contexts.

annotations.explanation: Show the different types of users who interact with the system, such as citizens, caseworkers, and administrators.
The main application services that deliver the solution's functionality.
Third-party systems and APIs the solution connects to, such as GOV.UK Notify or Pay.

walkthrough.instruction: Identify the key user groups and place them at the edges of your diagram.
Add the core application components in the centre, grouped logically by function.
Draw connections showing data flow and interactions between users, components, and external systems.

exercises.scenario: Design a solution overview for a case management system used by government caseworkers. The system integrates with GOV.UK Notify for emails and uses a cloud-hosted database.
hints: Include caseworkers and citizens as user groups
Show the case management application as the central component
Add GOV.UK Notify and the database as connected services

commonMistakes.description: Including too much technical detail in a solution overview
commonMistakes.incorrectExample: Showing individual microservices, database tables, and network subnets in the overview diagram
commonMistakes.correctedExample: Group related services into logical components and show only the major integration points
commonMistakes.explanation: Solution overview diagrams are for communicating the big picture. Technical detail belongs in lower-level diagrams such as deployment or data flow diagrams.
